title: Add a download-annotated-snapshot (PNG export) feature to the face detection demo
description:
Neither implementation (docker-app/public/app.js nor docker-app/src/index-wasm.js) offers any way to save or share a detection result -- confirmed via grep for toDataURL/download/snapshot/screenshot across both, zero matches. The app draws bounding boxes / landmarks / expression / age-gender labels onto a <canvas id="overlay"> layered over the <video> element (see docker-app/src/drawingUtils.js, landmarkDrawing.js) but that rendered result only ever exists live in the DOM.

For a face-detection demo, "detect my face, then save/share the annotated photo" is a natural, low-effort delight feature and a plausible source of organic sharing (screenshots of the annotated overlay are inherently more shareable than a live demo link).

Implementation sketch: on a user click (new "Save Snapshot" button next to the existing startBtn/stopBtn controls), composite the current <video> frame and the <canvas id="overlay"> content onto an offscreen canvas (drawImage video first, then drawImage the overlay canvas on top), then canvas.toDataURL("image/png") and trigger a download via a temporary <a download> link. No server round-trip needed -- everything is already client-side.

Files: docker-app/src/index-wasm.js (or docker-app/public/app.js if ADR-001/bf-68a has not landed yet when this is picked up) for the button + handler; docker-app/src/drawingUtils.js or landmarkDrawing.js may already expose reusable canvas-compositing helpers worth checking before writing new ones; docker-app/src/index.css / public/styles.css for button styling consistent with existing controls.

Acceptance: clicking "Save Snapshot" while detection is running downloads a PNG containing the current video frame with the detection overlay (boxes/landmarks/labels per active mode) burned in.

title: Author Argo WorkflowTemplate face-detection-build in declarative-config
description:
Create k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/face-detection-build-workflowtemplate.yml in jedarden/declarative-config (clone at ~/declarative-config; git pull --rebase before touching, push immediately after commit).

Model directly on palm-reading-build-workflowtemplate.yml (same repo shape: static CV demo container). Steps: resolve-version -> docker-build (kaniko) -> update-declarative-config.

Specifics for face-detection:
- WorkflowTemplate name: face-detection-build, namespace argo-workflows, serviceAccountName argo-workflow
- Params: git-repo=jedarden/face-detection, branch=main (NOT master)
- Dockerfile lives at docker-app/Dockerfile (NOT repo root). Kaniko args: --context=git://github.com/REPO.git#refs/heads/BRANCH --context-sub-path=docker-app --dockerfile=Dockerfile (see botburrow-agents-workflowtemplate.yml for --context-sub-path example; use workflow parameter templating as palm-reading does)
- Push destinations: ghcr.io/jedarden/face-detection:VERSION and :latest tag. Registry auth: mount secret ghcr-jedarden-registry (already exists in argo-workflows ns via ghcr-jedarden-registry-externalsecret.yml) as /kaniko/.docker (key .dockerconfigjson -> config.json), same volume pattern as palm-reading uses docker-hub-registry
- VERSION file does NOT exist in repo; resolve-version must initialize it at 2.0.2 (live deployment runs v2.0.1 image, env APP_VERSION=2.0.1) and commit it, per the palm-reading else-branch pattern. Git identity: user.email github@jedarden.com / user.name jedarden. GH_TOKEN from secret github-webhook-secret key token
- update-declarative-config step: sed image pin in k8s/ardenone-cluster/face-detection/face-detection-deployment.yml from current ghcr.io/jedarden/face-detection:latest to the new semver. NOTE the manifest currently uses :latest which violates repo policy; the sed must match any existing tag like palm template does. Optionally change imagePullPolicy Always to IfNotPresent in same commit
- Pin the kaniko executor image to a version tag (e.g. gcr.io/kaniko-project/executor:v1.23.2), NOT :latest. Newer templates must not add more :latest refs even though some older ones do
- Resources/retryStrategy/activeDeadlineSeconds: copy palm-reading values

Acceptance criteria:
1. File committed+pushed to declarative-config main
2. iad-ci templates sync via rs-manager ArgoCD; verify with kubectl --kubeconfig=/home/coding/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig get workflowtemplate face-detection-build -n argo-workflows
3. WorkflowTemplate exists on iad-ci cluster

Gap: doc-vs-artifact mismatch, not covered by any existing bead.

Evidence:
- README.md lines 15-19 document repository-structure section '1. /tools - YouTube Transcript Tools' (single/bulk/playlist transcript downloaders, Python).

- If the transcript scripts are meant to live here, add them under tools/ with a short README.

title: Add a service-worker precache for face-api.js model assets (instant repeat visits, offline-capable demo)
description:
The app is entirely client-side (webcam + browser-side TensorFlow.js/face-api.js inference, see docs/plan/plan.md for the full architecture summary) -- it has no server-side dependency once the static assets and ~6.8MB of face-api.js model files (docker-app/dist/models/, sizes: ssd_mobilenetv1 ~5.6MB, tiny_face_detector ~196KB, landmark68 ~357KB, expression ~330KB, age_gender ~430KB) are loaded. That makes it an unusually good fit for a service-worker precache: nothing about face detection requires network access after first load.

Currently every visit re-fetches models from the network (docker-app/nginx.conf does set 1y immutable Cache-Control on /models/, so repeat visits are HTTP-cache hits already, but a service worker precache would additionally make the whole app work offline after first visit, and load instantly on repeat visits even with a cold HTTP cache e.g. private/incognito browsing, cache eviction under storage pressure, or a first visit that only used Lite Mode -- see the related lazy-loading bead for why Pro Mode models may not be cached yet for a given visitor).

Work: add a minimal service worker (docker-app/public/sw.js or generated via a webpack plugin) that precaches the app shell (index.html, hashed JS/CSS bundles) and the /models/ directory contents on install, serves them cache-first on repeat visits, and is registered from the main entry point. Scope this to being purely additive/progressive-enhancement -- the app must continue to work normally with no service worker support or if registration fails.

Acceptance: after a first visit to https://face.jedarden.com (or a local build), a second visit with network disabled (devtools offline mode) still loads the app and successfully runs face detection against the webcam.

title: Lazy-load Pro-mode-only face-api.js models instead of eager-loading all 5 on page load
description:
Both existing implementations -- docker-app/public/app.js (legacy) and docker-app/src/index-wasm.js (current, see docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001) -- unconditionally load all five face-api.js model nets on DOMContentLoaded via Promise.all:
  tinyFaceDetector, ssdMobilenetv1, faceLandmark68Net, faceExpressionNet, ageGenderNet

Measured model sizes in this checkout (docker-app/dist/models/):
  tiny_face_detector: ~196KB (shard + manifest)
  ssd_mobilenetv1: ~4.2MB (shard1) + ~1.4MB (shard2) = ~5.6MB
  face_landmark_68: ~357KB
  face_expression: ~330KB
  age_gender: ~430KB
  Total: ~6.8MB

The app defaults to Lite Mode (the "lite" radio is checked by default in both public/app.js and the equivalent UI built by index-wasm.js), and Lite Mode only uses tinyFaceDetector per the README (bounding boxes only, 25-30 FPS target). ssdMobilenetv1 + landmarks + expression + age/gender (~6.6MB, ~97% of the total model payload) are Pro-Mode-only features that most visitors landing in the default mode never use, but pay the download/parse cost for anyway.

Fix: split model loading so only tinyFaceDetector loads eagerly on page load; load the remaining four nets on demand the first time the user switches to Pro Mode (with a loading indicator during that on-demand fetch, since it will take longer than switching modes in Lite-only usage).

Files: docker-app/src/index-wasm.js (model loading is inline in the FaceDetectionApp class, ~line 122-126) is the one to fix per ADR-001; if public/app.js still exists at the time this bead is picked up, apply the same split there too (~line 20-27).

Acceptance: initial page load only fetches tiny_face_detector_model-* from /models; ssd_mobilenetv1/face_landmark_68/face_expression/age_gender model requests only fire after switching to Pro Mode (verify via browser devtools Network tab or curl-based test).

title: Implement ADR-001: consolidate face-detection to a single self-hosted build path
description:
See docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 (2026-07-20) for full context/decision/alternatives.

Summary: docker-app ships two competing client entry points at once. docker-app/public/index.html loads face-api.js from cdn.jsdelivr.net plus docker-app/public/app.js (legacy, 627-line pre-webpack implementation), AND the webpack bundle built from docker-app/src/index-wasm.js (the intended WASM-accelerated path). Both attach DOMContentLoaded listeners, both eagerly fetch face-api.js models, both bind the same DOM element IDs (video/overlay/startBtn/stopBtn) -- confirmed against the actual built docker-app/dist/index.html. Whichever finishes last wins the DOM; the WASM optimization work has no reliable way to actually be what the user's session runs through.

Also docker-app/src/wasmBackend.js:15 loads the TF.js WASM binary from an unpinned CDN URL (.../@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm@latest/...) independent of the pinned ^4.22.0 in package.json.

Work:
1. Delete docker-app/public/app.js and the CDN face-api.js <script> tag from docker-app/public/index.html. @vladmandic/face-api (already imported by src/faceDetection.js and src/index-wasm.js) becomes the only face-api.js code path.
2. Vendor the TF.js WASM binaries at build time (already present under docker-app/node_modules/@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/dist/) via CopyWebpackPlugin in docker-app/webpack.common.js; point setWasmPaths() in docker-app/src/wasmBackend.js at the local path instead of the CDN @latest URL.
3. Remove cdn.jsdelivr.net / unpkg.com from the CSP script-src/style-src allowlist in docker-app/nginx.conf and docker-app/nginx.conf.template (they were added in commit 6e1a6c91 specifically to permit the CDN script tag being removed here).
4. Delete the now-redundant docker-app/src/*.pre-wasm snapshot files (faceDetection.js.pre-wasm, index.js.pre-wasm, proMode.js.pre-wasm) -- git history preserves them.
5. Re-run the existing Jest/Playwright suite (docker-app/tests/, docker-app/test-app-manual.js, docker-app/test-camera-selection.js, docker-app/verify-app.js) and update anything that was exercising the deleted public/app.js path specifically.

Acceptance: docker-app/dist/index.html after  contains exactly one face detection implementation (the hashed webpack bundle), no request to any *.jsdelivr.net or *.unpkg.com host at runtime, and docker-app/src/*.pre-wasm files are gone.

Note: independent of the existing Argo CI migration beads (bf-2jh/bf-2py/bf-vh3/bf-25r) in this same .beads workspace -- this fixes what gets shipped once that pipeline is working, not the pipeline itself.

comments.text: Correction: the description dropped a shell-substituted code span. The acceptance line should read: "docker-app/dist/index.html after running npm run build contains exactly one face detection implementation..." title: Wire Argo Events webhook trigger for face-detection (eventsource entry + sensor)
description:
Wire push-to-main triggering for the face-detection-build WorkflowTemplate, following the established jedarden.com/palm-reading pattern in jedarden/declarative-config.

Two changes in k8s/iad-ci/argo-events/:
1. Add a face-detection entry to github-eventsource.yml (EventSource github-webhooks, namespace argo-events): owner jedarden, names [face-detection], webhook endpoint /face-detection, port 12000, url https://webhooks-ci.ardenone.com, events [push], apiToken+webhookSecret from github-webhook-secret (keys token / webhook-secret), insecure false, active true, contentType json. Place under the Standalone container build repos section. The EventSource controller auto-creates the GitHub webhook on the repo using the apiToken — no manual GitHub configuration needed.
2. Create face-detection-sensor.yml modeled on palm-reading-sensor.yml: Sensor face-detection-sensor in argo-events ns, dependency on eventSourceName github-webhooks / eventName face-detection, filters: headers.X-Github-Event == push, body.ref == refs/heads/main (repo default branch is main, NOT master), and exclude CI auto-bump cascade (palm uses body.head_commit.author.name != Argo Workflows CI; the build commits as jedarden so prefer filtering body.head_commit.message prefix ci: auto-bump / ci: initialize VERSION via comparator if supported — at minimum replicate palm filter and verify no infinite build loop). Trigger: argoWorkflow submit, generateName face-detection-build-, workflowTemplateRef face-detection-build, params git-repo=jedarden/face-detection branch=main.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Both files committed+pushed to declarative-config main; ArgoCD syncs argo-events ns app on iad-ci
2. kubectl --kubeconfig=/home/coding/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig get sensor face-detection-sensor -n argo-events exists; eventsource pod restarts cleanly
3. GitHub webhook appears on jedarden/face-detection (gh api repos/jedarden/face-detection/hooks)
4. A test push to main produces a Workflow run (kubectl get workflows -n argo-workflows | grep face-detection)
